İtalya'da perşembe sabahı çok sayıda okul müdürüne yeni bir e-posta dalgasıyla bomba ihbarları gönderildi. İhbarlar üzerine bazı okullar tahliye edilirken, bazılarında ise yetkililer tarafından güvenlik kontrolleri gerçekleştirildi. E-postalar, çarşamba günü İtalya'da 6 bin okula gönderilen mesajlarda da kullanılan "Mikhail Andropov" adıyla imzalandı. Söz konusu okullarda öğrenciler ve okul personeli tahliye edildi.
İtalya Başbakanı Giorgia Meloni, yaşanan acil durumu görüşmek üzere perşembe sabahı hükümet temsilcilerini ve muhalefet liderlerini Roma'daki başbakanlık ofisi Palazzo Chigi'de toplantıya çağırdı.
Toplantıda Meloni'nin tüm siyasi partilere birlik içinde hareket etme çağrısında bulunduğu bildirildi. Meloni ayrıca Dışişleri Bakanı Antonio Tajani, Savunma Bakanı Guido Crosetto ve İçişleri Bakanı Matteo Piantedosi'nin parlamentoyu acilen bilgilendireceğini söyledi. Hükümet, bu tür tehditlere yönelik ortak bir protokol belirlemek amacıyla Cumhuriyet Güvenliği Bakanlıklararası Komitesi'nin (CISR) öğleden sonra toplanacağını açıkladı.
Hazırlanan protokol taslağına göre, tek tehlike işaretinin çok sayıda adrese gönderilen toplu bir e-posta olması halinde okulların tahliye edilmemesi öngörülüyor. Ancak her eyalette merkezi hükümeti temsil eden valiler, somut ve belirli risklerin bulunması durumunda tahliye kararı verme yetkisini koruyacak.
Toplantının ardından merkez sol Demokrat Parti'nin (PD) lideri Elly Schlein, "Görüşmenin yapılması olumlu ancak tartışmaların uygun platformlarda, yani parlamentoda ve Copasir'de sürdürülmesi gerekiyor," dedi.
İtalya'nın istihbarat servislerini denetleyen parlamento komitesi Copasir'e de atıfta bulunan Schlein, "Muhalefet olarak ülkeyi istikrarsızlaştırmayı ve kamuoyunda korku yaratmayı amaçlayan tehditler karşısında iş birliğine tamamen hazırız. Ancak hükümetin aldığı kararlara koşulsuz destek vermeyeceğiz. Bugün bize herhangi bir somut öneri sunulmadı," ifadelerini kullandı.
Yerel basında yer alan haberlere göre, bomba ihbarları nedeniyle perşembe günü Fransa'da da çok sayıda okul tahliye edildi. Bu gelişme, İtalya'nın da aralarında bulunduğu bazı Avrupa ülkelerindeki okulların benzer tehditler aldığı çarşamba gününün ardından yaşandı.
Fransa Eğitim Bakanlığı, Le Parisien gazetesine perşembe günü iki bomba ihbarı yapıldığını doğruladı. Bakanlık, olayların "geniş çaplı bir vakalar zinciri" oluşturduğu iddiasını ise reddetti.
Fransa'nın güneyindeki Marsilya kentinde bulunan Don Bosco Lisesi, saat 09.00 sıralarında tahliye edildi. La Provence gazetesinin haberine göre, öğle saatlerinden kısa süre sonra polis ekipleri ve bomba imha uzmanları, patlayıcı tespit köpeğiyle birlikte okulda inceleme yaptı.
Fransa'nın doğusundaki Jura Dağları'nda bulunan Morez kasabasında ise Victor-Bérard Lisesi, okul yönetiminin e-posta yoluyla gönderilen "endişe verici bir mesaj" olarak nitelendirdiği ihbarın ardından tahliye edildi. Yakındaki bir ortaokul da boşaltılırken bölgeye bomba imha ekipleri sevk edildi.
Fransa'nın kuzeyindeki Laon kentinde bulunan Teknoloji Enstitüsü de perşembe sabahı yapılan bomba ihbarı nedeniyle tahliye edildi.
Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron, Avrupa genelinde son dönemde artan ve uçuşları da hedef alan asılsız bomba ihbarlarının arkasında "yabancı güçlerin" bulunup bulunmadığını söylemek için henüz erken olduğunu belirtti.
İrlanda'nın başkenti Dublin'de düzenlenen Avrupa liderleri toplantısı sırasında gazetecilere konuşan Macron, "Şu an itibarıyla sorumluların kimliğini belirlememizi sağlayacak yeterli veriye sahip değiliz. Bu çağrıların arkasında yabancı güçlerin bulunup bulunmadığını söyleyemeyiz," dedi.

Tech giant’s market value drops below $4 trillion after Huang steps down following espionage and affair allegations.
Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of tech giant Nvidia following his reported affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a company executive.
The firm’s market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025 following the announcement, capping a volatile week as Huang’s scandals rocked the company, which supplies most of the chips powering advanced artificial intelligence (AI) technology. The stock slid roughly 10 percent in early trading as US markets opened on Thursday. The tech-heavy Nasdaq was down 0.6 percent.
The company appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer and executive vice president, as interim CEO on Thursday.
The firm also added its first-ever board chair, Harvey C Jones, who has been a venture investor for the last three decades.
Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday night to discuss ousting Huang, whose relationship with an alleged Chinese spy triggered investigations by the FBI, the United States Congress and the California-based chip maker. Nvidia is also facing a shareholder class-action lawsuit.
The alleged Chinese intelligence asset, Alice Huang, is a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, Nvidia’s primary business partner in Southeast Asia. Founded in 2023, Megaspeed has been investigated over whether it helped Chinese companies access its $4.8bn stock of powerful Nvidia chips.
The affair has raised national security concerns in the US, which restricts chip sales to China over concerns that the Chinese military, intelligence agencies or companies could use the advanced technology.
Huang, 63, is Nvidia’s cofounder, president and CEO. A close ally of US President Donald Trump, he has pushed to ease US restrictions on chip exports to China. Trump said earlier this week that Huang told him he had “absolutely no idea” that he was in a relationship with an intelligence operative.
Huang owns about 3.6 percent of Nvidia’s stock, making him one of the richest people in the world. He is a powerful figure in the AI industry, which has driven record stock market and wider economic gains. The company is set to report quarterly earnings on Tuesday.
Aleksandar Tomic, associate dean for strategy, innovation, and technology at Boston College, told Al Jazeera that the “resignation of Jensen Huang will have an outsized effect compared to a similar event at another large corporation given the relatively flat structure of Nvidia.”
But he said that Nvidia, an AI bellwether, “is in a very strong position” that will enable the company to transition from Huang’s leadership. Tomic called Huang’s resignation a “speed bump” for the company.
“Nvidia is a strong company with a strong product and this is a sudden event, not a product of corporate struggle,” he said. “It may take some time to figure out the succession process, but Nvidia can handle it as they approach it from the position of strength.”
Nvidia’s board, which hired a law firm to investigate the affair with Alice Huang, met to decide Huang’s fate on Wednesday shortly after The New York Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia vice president who reports to him.
Nvidia’s stock has tumbled since the scandal erupted, falling to a 14-year low, the Reuters news agency reported.

Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB) Başkanı Fatih Karahan, 12 Kasım 2026'da yılın dördüncü ve son Enflasyon Raporu'nu açıkladı. Sunumda 2026 yıl sonu enflasyon tahmini yüzde 28'den yüzde 29,5'e yükseltilirken 2027 ve 2028 yıllarına ilişkin beklentilerde de yukarı yönlü güncellemeye gidildi. Karahan, enerji fiyatlarındaki artış ve jeopolitik gelişmelerin enflasyon görünümü üzerindeki etkilerine dikkat çekerek sıkı para politikası duruşunun sürdürüleceğini bildirdi. Peki, TCMB'nin yeni enflasyon tahminleri kaç oldu? İşte, 2026 yıl sonu enflasyon beklentisi…
TCMB'nin yeni Enflasyon Raporu'na göre 2026 yıl sonu enflasyon tahmini yüzde 28'den yüzde 29,5'e çıkarıldı. Böylece Merkez Bankası, yıl sonu enflasyon öngörüsünü 1,5 puan yukarı yönlü revize etti.
TCMB Başkanı Fatih Karahan, enerji fiyatlarındaki yükselişin ve jeopolitik gelişmelerin enflasyon görünümünü etkilediğini belirtti. Hürmüz Boğazı üzerinden enerji sevkiyatının normalleşmesine ilişkin beklentilerin zayıflaması ve bölgedeki gerilimlerin artması nedeniyle 2026 ve 2027 yıllarına ilişkin petrol fiyatı varsayımlarının da yükseltildiğini açıkladı.
Merkez Bankası, gelecek yıllara ilişkin enflasyon tahminlerinde de artışa gitti. Bir önceki Enflasyon Raporu'nda 2027 yıl sonu için yüzde 15, 2028 yıl sonu için yüzde 9 olarak açıklanan tahminler yukarı yönlü güncellendi.
Yeni rapora göre TCMB'nin yıllara göre enflasyon tahminleri şöyle:
Fatih Karahan, enflasyon görünümünü etkileyen unsurlar arasında enerji fiyatlarındaki yükseliş ve jeopolitik gelişmeleri gösterdi. Eylül ve ekim aylarında ham petrol ve doğal gaz fiyatlarında belirgin artış yaşandığını belirten Karahan, yüksek enerji fiyatlarının küresel enflasyon ve enflasyon beklentileri üzerindeki etkisinin sürdüğünü ifade etti.
Karahan, gıda enflasyonunun arz koşullarındaki iyileşmeyle gerilediğini ancak oynak seyrini koruduğunu söyledi. Hizmet enflasyonundaki yavaşlamanın yıl boyunca devam ettiğini, temel mal enflasyonunun ise düşük seyrini sürdürdüğünü kaydetti. Kira enflasyonundaki yavaşlama eğiliminin belirginleştiğine de dikkat çekti.
TCMB, enflasyonun önümüzdeki yıllarda kademeli olarak gerilemesini öngörüyor. Başkan Fatih Karahan'ın açıkladığı tahminlere göre enflasyonun 2029 yıl sonunda yüzde 9'a düşmesi, orta vadede ise yüzde 5 seviyesinde istikrar kazanması bekleniyor.
Karahan, fiyat istikrarı sağlanana kadar sıkı para politikası duruşunun sürdürüleceğini vurguladı. Enflasyonun ara hedeflerle uyumlu şekilde gerilemesini sağlamak amacıyla para politikası kararlarında risklerin ve enflasyon beklentilerinin dikkate alınmaya devam edileceğini belirtti.

texts.https://www.wired.com/story/nvidia-ceo-j:
Jensen Huang stepped down as the chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, four days after the company announced its internal investigation into an affair he had with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
“Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately,” the Nvidia board said in a statement. Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO. The board said it “will consider internal and external candidates” for a permanent replacement.
The board’s investigation was announced on November 8, slightly less than two weeks after The New York Times reported that the chief executive had been the target of a Chinese intelligence operation facilitated through his relationship with Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen. The pair have been spotted in public together at least twice, in June 2024 and May 2025 . On November 11, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also allegedly had a relationship with a direct report at Nvidia.
The alleged relationship with a subordinate, along with Huang’s business dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company where Alice Huang previously held a senior position, likely played a greater role in the board’s decision to oust Huang than the Chinese espionage allegations, a source familiar with the matter tells WIRED.
US intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump on Huang’s relationship with Alice last year, but the president did not act on it. On November 6, The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Alice was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security and that she had been recruited to collect information on the Nvidia executive. (The Chinese government has rejected all claims that Alice was a spy for the country. )
Huang sent a companywide email on Sunday acknowledging his affair, apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees, and pledging cooperation with the internal investigation. The executive has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, since 1985 , and both of the couple’s two children work at the company.
On Monday, WIRED exclusively reported that last year Huang began working with a crisis PR firm to manage his personal communications. In October 2025, those PR consultants started to be looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang, whether those inquiries were personal or professional in nature.
The timing lines up with a New York Times report that month that the US Commerce Department was investigating whether Alice Huang’s Megaspeed was helping Chinese companies get around American export controls with the help of a vast web of subsidiaries. The investigation was reportedly halted and transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter inquired about it.
Huang has been a vocal critic of these export controls, which he argues unnecessarily constrain the market for American chips, create discrete Chinese and American tech ecosystems, and spur China to build competitive chips of its own. Huang has worked to develop a relationship with Trump in order to advocate for policies that are advantageous for Nvidia, including the idea of opening its markets to China.
Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with friends Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. The trio reportedly brainstormed their vision for the company in a Denny’s diner and aspired to bring realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For the first few decades of its existence, Nvidia was primarily known in the gaming community for creating chips powerful enough to render high-quality in-game graphics.
In 2012, after a new kind of neural network known as AlexNet won a high-profile prize in computer vision, Nvidia pivoted from high-speed computer graphics to building chips that would support artificial intelligence. Huang has repeatedly said that the introduction of AlexNet, which was developed by AI engineers Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton, was a “Big Bang”–like event for computing.
Because its new GPUs proved highly effective at powering AI models that require massive amounts of processing power, the value of Nvidia shares soared in 2023 and 2024, in lockstep with the broader AI boom that began sweeping through the world economy. In the summer of 2025, Nvidia became the first company in history to cross $4 trillion in value.
As of September 2026, the company controlled about 90 percent of the GPU market. Much of Nvidia’s epic rise over the few decades has been attributed not just to its cutting-edge chips and its software “moat,” CUDA, that keeps developers locked into those chips, but also to the fast-thinking, controlling, charismatic, and often bombastic leadership style of Huang himself. Now, that critical part of the company’s success is out.

texts.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nvidia:
Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as president and chief executive of Nvidia, the company said on Thursday, just a few days after he admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy, sparking a U.S. national security crisis.
In a regulatory filing , Nvidia said its board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday.
Nvidia said its current chief financial officer and executive vice president, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO until the company finds a permanent successor. Kress will continue to serve as the company’s CFO.
Nvidia’s shares were down nearly 12% in early morning trading on Thursday. Since Friday, the company’s stock has fallen by as much as 19%, resulting in a market cap loss of more than $855 billion.
Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it as CEO ever since. Under his leadership, Nvidia played a crucial role in developing the graphics processing unit (GPU), a specialized chip that does graphics processing for PCs, as we know it today. The chips were not an immediate hit, and the early days of Nvidia were characterized by struggle and layoffs, but eventually, it struck on a GPU design that performed so well, it became the standard for graphics processing.
These chips also turned out to be extremely good at doing large numbers of calculations simultaneously, which has made them popular for computation-intensive tasks like crypto mining, and more recently, training and running neural networks, which are what AI models are at their core.
Nvidia was initially focused on making GPUs aimed at gaming, but it had already moved into general-purpose computing by 2006 with the launch of the CUDA architecture, which lets developers use the chips for other tasks, such as doing calculations and research. After AI researchers began using the company’s GPUs to train neural networks over a decade ago, Huang leaned in toward developing chips for AI and then data centers, and grew it from there into its dominant position.
Under Huang, the company has been by far the biggest beneficiary of the AI industry’s skyrocketing growth, which has largely depended on Nvidia’s GPUs for training and running large language models. Before ChatGPT launched and sparked the AI boom, Nvidia shares were trading at about $15. As of last month, they had risen more than 1,450% to an all-time high of $243. Its market cap consequently has also risen by an eye-watering $5.5 trillion since then, reaching as high as $5.88 trillion early in October.
Revenue, of course, has also ballooned, rising more than 1,500% to $96.22 billion as of the company’s second quarter, from $5.93 billion in Q3 2023, right before the ChatGPT moment. Profits increased nearly 88 times in that period to $59.69 billion as of July 2026, from $680 million in October 2023.
That success was predicated on large part by the AI industry’s continued development, which Huang seemingly made his personal mission. He traveled to conferences and events around the world to promote his products and AI, lobbied extensively for looser regulation after the Biden administration placed export controls on the sale of high-power AI chips to China, and cultivated a close relationship with Trump, often to Nvidia’s benefit .
The resignation and controversy come at a crucial moment for Nvidia. China was always a big market for the company, though its impact on the company’s finances has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. Chinese customers accounted for revenue of about $7.9 billion in the company’s second quarter, roughly 8% of total revenue.
The potential implications of Huang’s departure for the AI and data center industries are vast, given how active Huang, and by extension Nvidia, has been in furthering the AI boom. In particular, it raises questions about the future of Nvidia’s sprawling AI investments, which have helped bankroll everything from startups developing new technologies to the enormous data centers needed to run them.
Under Huang, Nvidia deftly used its financial muscle to support companies buying its chips, effectively helping to finance the market for its own products, as well as lobbying Washington to relax potential rules around AI and data center regulation.
As of the end of its second quarter, Nvidia reported $99 billion worth of investments and another $25 billion of commitments. It also has $36 billion in cloud service commitments, which are arrangements that help AI cloud operators finance the GPUs and data center equipment they buy from Nvidia, with the chipmaker saying it will buy compute from them and potentially earn a share of their operators’ revenue.
Nvidia has also been investing directly in neoclouds, the companies serving a lot of the AI processing needs. In January, the company invested $2 billion in CoreWeave , and another $2 billion in Nebius in March. The chipmaker was said to be considering being a guarantor for Nscale’s planned West Virginia data center project. It’s also signed up to provide up to $105 billion worth of credit guarantees for an OpenAI data center campus in Ohio.
Nvidia’s also a major investor in the labs building the AI models that run on its GPUs, putting $30 billion into OpenAI, and $10 billion into Anthropic . It’s also backed Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab as part of a deal involving at least 1 GW of its Vera Rubin GPU systems. The chipmaker has also invested $3.5 billion in MediaTek to help the Taiwanese company develop custom AI chips that work with Nvidia’s systems.
Many investors have grown uneasy with the enormous amounts of debt companies in the space were raising to sustain the AI infrastructure buildout, and Huang’s exit throws another uncertainty-shaped wrench into the works. CoreWeave’s shares were down about 9% on Thursday, reversing part of a 25% rally on Wednesday, while Nebius is down about 16%. IREN fell 6.6%.
Nvidia’s board has also appointed Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. As chair, Jones is likely to play a central role in Nvidia’s search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang.
Huang is the single largest personal shareholder at Nvidia, but he owns only about 3.5% of the company’s shares. Unlike many of Silicon Valley’s tech giants, he does not hold supervoting rights, and the board had the power to vote him out at any time.
Huang famously ran a very flat organization, with around 60 direct reports. There was no heir apparent or succession plan either (although two of his children also worked in executive roles at the company). Huang famously maintained tight control over the company he founded, making it challenging for Nvidia to find a path forward without him.
The industry will get its first glimpse of that next week during the quarterly conference call. Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.
“Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the company said in a statement.
Note: This story was updated to add details about Nvidia’s growth and Huang’s efforts to promote AI development, as well as its focus on China.

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of AI giant Nvidia on Thursday, the company said, after revelations he had two extramarital affairs , including one with a woman accused of spying for China .
Huang's resignation leaves the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouds ​the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse.
Read more Nvidia board weighs ouster of CEO Jensen Huang amid spy scandal
Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor, ending Huang's 33-year run at the helm of the global juggernaut he co-founded.
Huang, 63, also gave up his seat on the board. The company did not give a reason for his departure.
The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its founding leader at a crucial time for the sector.
Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in premarket trading Thursday following the announcement. The stock was already down around 25 percent from its all-time high in early October.
The board said it had appointed Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as its first-ever chair.
"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Jones said in a statement.
Kress said she was committed to "building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years".
Jensen Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related.
US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China's Ministry of State Security.
On Sunday, Nvidia's board announced a probe into what it called reporting that Huang had been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort", while saying it retained confidence in him.
On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that Huang had a second extramarital affair, citing video evidence of him being affectionate with Nvidia's vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell.
Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia's efforts to expand its technology into higher education and health care. She was speaking at a conference in San Jose, California, where the two "were seen being affectionate at the hotel" by bystanders, the Times reported.
Nvidia's code of conduct tells employees to avoid conflicts of interest and cites the example of "personal relationships".
Nvidia shareholders have filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the company for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors.
Huang had repeatedly avoided naming a successor when the question was raised.
Kress joined Nvidia as finance chief in 2013 after nearly 25 years in finance roles at companies including Cisco and Microsoft.
Founded in 1993, Nvidia designs graphics processing units (GPUs), components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games that have become the backbone of AI systems.
Its processors are mostly made by Taiwanese company TSMC, the world's largest contract manufacturer of chips.
Nvidia said it would release its quarterly results as scheduled on November 17.

United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf, citing a risk to cybersecurity and undermining federal regulations.
The airline is the latest American corporate giant to prevent customers from using AI agents and autonomous assistants to access their systems. The move comes as airlines and banks are struggling to differentiate between real customers and AI systems operating on their behalf, such as when users share their logins with their AI assistants. Sharing passwords with apps and assistants can create security risks if those credentials get leaked or exposed.
United warns that “sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles.”
The airline also warns of a risk of violating federal aviation rules, such as requiring that a human completes flight check-ins to acknowledge that their bags do not contain banned substances.
“As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants,” the airline said in a statement . “This work includes updates to our booking, ticketing and distribution policies.”
The airline’s move follows a warning from banks, including Bank of America, which last week urged customers not to share their passwords with their AI assistants.

texts.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/nectar:
Nectar , an AI-powered operating system for marketing, is launching a new AI agent designed to take a lot of the manual work out of influencer marketing, from finding the right creators to contacting them, managing partnerships, and tracking results.
Founded by sisters Misbah and Farah Uraizee, both former Meta employees, Nectar came out of stealth last year and uses AI agents to help brands manage social media, customer conversations, content moderation, creator partnerships, and competitor research.
Announced Thursday, its new “Creator Agent” can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations, and monitor how campaigns perform. Instead of having marketing teams spend weeks scrolling through social media, building spreadsheets, and sending individual DMs, Nectar wants its agent to handle much of that work automatically.
Nectar joins other companies introducing agentic AI assistants designed to automate influencer outreach, including Aspire and GRIN . The launch also comes as more brands turn to creators to reach customers. U.S. spending on creator advertising is expected to reach $44 billion in 2026, according to the Interactive Advertising Bureau . As companies work with hundreds or even thousands of creators, keeping track of relationships and measuring results can get pretty difficult.
Nectar says its Creator Agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles to find potential partners, including smaller creators who may not yet have a large following but are gaining traction. The system analyzes videos to understand what creators post about, how their content fits a brand, and whether their previous partnerships are appropriate. It also checks brand safety by reviewing content in context rather than simply searching for specific keywords.
Nectar then creates ranked lists of recommendations and adds new matches as creators become more popular.
Once it finds a potential match, the agent can draft and send messages in a brand’s voice, create custom landing pages to collect creator information, and help manage contracts, product gifting, and shipping details. It also remembers previous conversations and interactions, so brands can keep track of relationships without relying on spreadsheets.
“Brands can share voice guidelines in any format, and Nectar picks up the rest from their history,” CEO Misbah Uraizee tells TechCrunch. “On top of that sits a set of proprietary guardrails that keep every draft on tone and in context. Nectar understands what is being said in a video, reads the tone of the conversation, and knows the difference between a quote post on X and a TikTok comment section. A brand should not sound identical in both, and with Nectar it doesn’t.”
Another feature looks for personal milestones in creators’ lives, such as an engagement, a new baby, or completing a marathon. The agent can then suggest a personalized message or gift, helping brands build relationships that feel less like one-off advertising deals.
Creator Agent is available today globally and covers Instagram creators and TikTokers.
The company plans to make the agent available through its Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing teams to use it through AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, as well as their own custom-built agents.
This past May, Nectar raised a $30 million Series A round led by Menlo Ventures and its Anthology Fund, which is a joint initiative launched with Anthropic.

Oxford Üniversitesi Robotics Institute araştırmacısı Walter Goodwin tarafından kurulan Fractile, yapay zeka modellerinin çıkarım (inference) süreçlerinde ihtiyaç duyduğu işlem gücünü sağlamak üzere özel çipler geliştiriyor. Çıkarım süreci, bir yapay zeka modelinin eğitiminin ardından kullanıcıdan gelen bir komutu veya soruyu işleyerek yanıt üretmesini ifade ediyor. Bu süreçte modellerin büyük miktarda veriyi hızlı bir şekilde işlemesi gerekiyor.
Fractile de tam bu noktada devreye girerek, yapay zeka modellerinin daha kısa sürede yanıt üretmesini sağlayacak donanımlar üzerinde çalışıyor. Şirketin geliştirdiği çipler, özellikle yapay zeka modellerinin çalıştırılması sırasında ortaya çıkan yüksek işlem maliyetlerini ve enerji tüketimini azaltmayı hedefliyor.
Fractile, mevcut donanımlara kıyasla daha hızlı çıkarım performansı sunarak yapay zeka uygulamalarının daha verimli çalışmasını amaçlıyor. Nvidia gibi şirketlerin öne çıktığı yapay zeka donanımı pazarında alternatif bir teknoloji geliştirmeye odaklanan girişim, ilk ticari ürününü 2027 yılında kullanıma sunmayı hedefliyor.

Çiftçi, Konya'nın irfanının asırlardır insanlara gönül incitmemeyi, hoşgörülü olmayı, komşusunun halini sormayı, eli ve gönlü açık olmayı öğütlediğini belirterek, şunları söyledi:
"Biz bu güzel ahlakı büyüklerimizin, komşumuzun, esnafımızın davranışlarında ve ihtimamında hep gördük. Çocuklarımıza bırakacağımız en kıymetli miras da bu kadim ahlaktır. Konyalı şairimiz Feyzi Halıcı, Konya'mıza duyduğu sevgiyi ne güzel dile getiriyor. 'Tarihin yüreği, can beldesidir, asırla ölçülmez yaşı Konya'nın. İç Anadolu'nun şan beldesidir, dünyada bulunmaz eşi Konya'nın. Çoktan kuraklığa çekildi bir set, taşar tarlalarda feyiz, bereket. Fezai beş vakit Rabbe dua et, bol olsun ekmeği, aşı Konya'nın.' Rabbim Konya'mızın toprağına bereket, hanelerine huzur nasip eylesin."
Tanıtım günleri boyunca Konya'nın lezzetlerini tadacaklarını, sanatkarların el emeğini göreceklerini, türkülerini dinleyeceklerini dile getiren Çiftçi, "Belki bir çocuğumuz ilk defa bir ustanın elinden çıkan esere yakından bakacak, bir gencimiz ailesinden dinlediği memleket hikayesinin izini sürecektir. İstanbul'da evlatlarına Konya'yı anlatan, onlara büyüklerinin hatırasını ve memleket sevgisini aktaran bütün hemşehrilerime gönülden teşekkür ediyorum. Bizlere düşen, bu mirası korurken Konya'mızın üretimine, istihdamına ve huzuruna da hep birlikte sahip çıkmaktır." ifadelerini kullandı.
Çiftçi, "Muhterem Cumhurbaşkanımız Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın liderliğinde Türkiye Yüzyılı'nı inşa ederken çiftçimizin tarlasına, esnafımızın dükkanına, evlatlarımızın okuluna gönül rahatlığıyla gidebilmesi için gayretle çalışıyoruz. İçişleri Bakanlığı olarak Konya'mızın ve ülkemizin her köşesinin huzur ve güvenliğini aynı hassasiyetle gözetiyoruz." diye konuştu.
Bakan Çiftçi, millete hizmet yolunda dur durak bilmeden çalışmaya devam edeceklerini söyledi.
Suç ve suçluyla kararlı şekilde mücadeleyi sürdürdüklerini vurgulayan Çiftçi, "Mücadelemizi yalnızca sınırlarımız içerisinde yapmayıp, dünyanın her yerinde ülkemizde suç işlemiş, vatandaşımıza zarar vermiş çetelerin de peşini bırakmayacağız." dedi.
"Yıl başından bugüne kadar 45 ülkeden, 189'u çete elebaşı veya üyesi olmak üzere 805 firariyi bugün itibarıyla ülkemize getirmiş durumdayız. Bugün de basından takip etmiş olmalısınız. Kırmızı bültenle ülkemizde aranan ve Yunanistan'a kaçmış olan yeni nesil suç örgütü liderini bugün Yunanistan'dan getirdik ve adalete teslim ettik. Bu yıl içerisinde toplamda 669 organize suç örgütüne 1951 operasyon yaptık, inşallah bundan sonra da yapmaya devam edeceğiz. Bunların faaliyet alanlarını daraltmaya, bunların kökünü kesmeye sizlerin de desteğiyle elimizden geldiği kadar çabalayacağız, gayret edeceğiz."
Aynı azim ve kararlılıkla mücadelelerine bundan sonra da devam edeceklerini belirten Çiftçi, "Bu sene içerisinde yurt dışında kırmızı bültenle aradığımız kişilerin sayısını, Türkiye'ye getireceğimiz kişilerin sayısını inşallah 1000 olarak belirledik ve bu hedefimize de ulaşacağız." dedi.
"Sokak eşkıyalarına buradan bir çağrım var, kaçtığınız yer değişebilir ama hesap vereceğiniz yer kesinlikle değişmeyecek. Devletimizin hafızası güçlü, iradesi sarsılmazdır. Milletimizin huzuruna, canına ve malına kastedenler bilsin ki dünyanın hiçbir köşesi kendileri için güvenli bir sığınak değildir. Suç işleyip kaçmayı kurtuluş sananları saklandıkları inlerden tek tek bulup adaletin karşısına çıkaracak ve onların hepsinin burnunu teker teker süreceğiz inşallah. Bu kararlı mücadelede emeği için kahraman polislerimizi, jandarmamızı, ilgili birimlerimizi tebrik ediyor, Adalet Bakanımıza da huzurlarınızda teşekkür ediyorum. Türkiye'nin huzuruna uzanan hiçbir el, devletimizin erişemeyeceği kadar uzakta değildir. "

Report: Ukraine suspects speeds limits are intended to help Russia in peace talks.
Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said today that Starshield has again been disabled on fast-moving drones in Ukrainian territory occupied by Russian forces, and that the US has provided “very little” information about the return of the restriction.
“We have detected speed restrictions on Starshield on our Ukrainian territory again, in the temporarily occupied parts of Ukraine,” Zelenskyy said in a speech at the 9th European Political Community Summit in Ireland. “The speed limit is back at 161 kilometers per hour—that’s 100 miles per hour.”
Zelenskyy’s allegation is that Starshield—the military variant of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite service—stops working on Ukrainian military drones when they travel above 161 kilometers per hour.
SpaceX today denied Zelenskyy’s allegation. “This is false. There has been no change,” SpaceX’s media relations department told Ars today when asked if SpaceX has any response to Zelenskyy’s statement that Starshield is being restricted again.
SpaceX has received multiple Pentagon contracts to give Ukraine access to the military-focused Starshield. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said last month that any decisions on Starshield restrictions are made by the US government. The Pentagon inspector general’s office has since declined a request from US senators to investigate who ordered the restrictions.
Ukraine officials reportedly said today that they believe the limit was reinstated to put pressure on Ukraine in the latest round of peace talks with Russia. Zelenskyy said in today’s speech that without satellite connectivity on its drones, Ukraine cannot intercept Russian drones that fly in from the occupied parts of Ukraine.
It has often been unclear whether US and Ukrainian government officials discussing the restrictions were referring to Starlink, the civilian service that isn’t supposed to be used for offensive military purposes, or Starshield, which relies on the same technology but is intended for military use. But today, Zelenskyy clearly stated that the current restrictions affect Starshield.
“This directly affects our ability to intercept Russian jet-powered Shahed drones,” Zelenskyy said. “These drones come from those [occupied] areas, and because of the speed restrictions, we simply cannot catch up with them in time. Near the front line, we cannot use our aircraft. Only drone interceptors can operate there. And without the speed we need, shooting down these Shaheds becomes much harder. This means more Russian strikes get through, and more of our people are killed, our civilians are killed, by Russia.”
Ukraine officials reported the first round of restrictions about a month ago , but the limits were removed by October 24. Zelenskyy said today that Ukraine doesn’t know why the limit is in place again.
“We are trying to get the details from the American side, but so far we know very little,” Zelenskyy said. “But some things are very clear. If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going. We need to be clear and never recognize Russia’s occupation of Ukrainian territory in any way.”
A Financial Times article today described Ukrainian officials’ allegations that the Starshield limit was put back in place to influence peace talks:
Senior Ukrainian officials told the FT they believed the speed restrictions were imposed in an effort to pressure Kyiv during the latest peace talks with Russia, which just concluded in Abu Dhabi. US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, were in Moscow on Thursday to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, after which they were set to travel to Ireland to meet Zelenskyy. One senior Ukrainian official said it appeared that Washington wanted to strengthen Russia’s position in the talks.
“These are not random errors, but systematic speed restrictions,” Zelenskyy said. “For us, this primarily means a significant complication in intercepting Russian jet-powered drones.”
Musk last month accused Ukraine of using the Starlink commercial service for offensive drone strikes, which he said violates the terms of service. A Ukraine official denied Musk’s accusation and said previous limits imposed by SpaceX already prevented Ukraine’s military from using the commercial Starlink service in the way Musk described.
As for the Starshield military variant, Musk has said that “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.” Trump denied making the decision to limit Ukraine’s satellite connectivity, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the administration had “no foreknowledge” of the slowdown.
We contacted the White House today and will update this article if we get a response. European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said that restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Starshield are unacceptable.
“It is not the first time that Ukraine is facing Starshield disruptions. These reports are deeply concerning and, if confirmed, unacceptable,” Regnier said at a press conference. “SpaceX must have a consistent approach in sharing its services with Ukraine. Starshield services must be restored urgently for Ukraine to keep its soldiers connected, to protect its citizens, and to defend its territory.”

Yapay zeka destekli veri analitiği girişimi Edelbyte , iki yatırım turunda toplam 70 milyon dolar yatırım aldı. 25 milyon dolarlık tohum yatırım turuna Sequoia Capita l liderlik ederken Greenoaks ve Swish Ventures da tura katıldı.
2025 yılında kurulan şirketin 45 milyon dolarlık A serisi turuna ise Quiet Capital liderlik etti. Turda ayrıca mevcut yatırımcıların yanı sıra QP Ventures, Startpoint Capital ve Cerca Partners yer aldı.
500 milyon dolar değerlemeye ulaşan şirket, yeni yatırımı müşteri tabanını genişletmek ve ekibini büyütmek için kullanacağını açıkladı.
Edelbyte, Avner Aharoni , Evgeney Ryzhyk , Alexander Sloutsky ve Yoni Leibowitz tarafından kuruldu. Platform, şirketlerin büyük ölçekli verilerini depolamasını, aramasını ve analiz etmesini sağlayan, yapay zeka ajanları için optimize edilmiş bir veri analitiği platformu geliştiriyor. Snowflake ve Databricks'e alternatif olarak konumlanan platform, yüzlerce petabayta kadar veriyi tek bir ortamda yönetebiliyor. Standart veri kayıtlarının yanı sıra yapay zeka ajanlarının kullandığı vektör verilerini de destekliyor.
Platform, arama, iş zekası ve grafik işleme gibi farklı analitik ihtiyaçlarını tek bir altyapıda karşılıyor. Şirketlerin verilerini analiz etmek için farklı bir işlem ortamına taşımasına gerek bırakmayan Edelbyte, sorguları verilerin halihazırda saklandığı sistemlerde çalıştırabiliyor. Böylece veri aktarımını azaltırken analiz süreçlerini hızlandırmayı hedefliyor. Edelbyte, büyük veri kümelerinde sorguların daha hızlı gerçekleştirilmesi için indeksleme ve çeşitli optimizasyon yöntemlerinden yararlanıyor.
Şirket, platformunun çok petabaytlık veri kümelerinde 100 milisaniyenin altında gecikmeyle sorgulama yapabildiğini belirtiyor. Özellikle yapay zeka uygulamalarının ihtiyaç duyduğu büyük ve karmaşık veri sorgularını daha hızlı ve verimli hale getirmeyi amaçlıyor.

Amazon Türkiye, yapay zeka destekli alışveriş asistanı Alexa ile Alışveriş 'i (Alexa for Shopping) beta sürümüyle Türkiye'deki kullanıcıların erişimine açtı. Amazon Türkiye mobil uygulaması ve Amazon.com.tr üzerinden kullanılabilen özellik, kullanıcıların ürün araştırmasına, farklı seçenekleri karşılaştırmasına ve ihtiyaçlarına göre öneriler almasına yardımcı oluyor.
Amazon hesabında oturum açmış tüm kullanıcıların ücretsiz olarak erişebildiği Alexa ile Alışveriş, doğal dilde gerçekleştirilen sohbetler üzerinden çalışıyor. Kullanıcılar yeni bir ürün kategorisini araştırırken nelere dikkat etmeleri gerektiğini Alexa'ya sorabiliyor ya da belirli kriterlere göre ürün önerileri isteyebiliyor.
Örneğin yeni bir ürün kategorisini araştıran kullanıcılar kapasite, güç ve kullanım kolaylığı gibi kriterler hakkında bilgi alabiliyor. Hediye arayan kullanıcılar yaş ve ilgi alanı gibi bilgiler üzerinden önerilere ulaşabilirken, iki farklı ürün arasında karar vermeye çalışanlar ürünlerin özelliklerini, fiyatlarını ve müşteri yorumlarında öne çıkan noktaları karşılaştırabiliyor.
Alexa ile Alışveriş'in beta sürümü, Amazon Türkiye'deki ürün bilgileri ve milyonlarca müşteri yorumunun yanı sıra internet genelindeki verilerden de yararlanıyor. Amazon'a göre sistem bu bilgileri bir araya getirerek kullanıcıların alışveriş kararlarını kolaylaştırmayı amaçlıyor.
Amazon Türkiye'nin Veri Enstitüsü'ne yaptırdığı E-Ticaret Standartları Endeksi araştırması da şirketin yeni özelliği kullanıma sunduğu dönemde tüketicilerin yapay zekaya yaklaşımına ilişkin veriler paylaşıyor. 2026 yılının Ağustos ayında Türkiye'yi temsil eden 2 bin 530 kişilik bir örneklemle gerçekleştirilen araştırmaya göre, son altı ayda online alışveriş yapan tüketicilerin yüzde 50'si yapay zeka destekli alışveriş özelliklerini kullanmaya açık olduğunu belirtiyor. Kullanıcıların yapay zekadan en çok fayda beklediği alanlar ise yüzde 33 ile fiyat takibi ve yüzde 27 ile müşteri yorumlarının özetlenmesi olarak öne çıkıyor.
Amazon Türkiye Ülke Müdürü Burak Erdem , Alexa ile Alışveriş deneyiminin dünya genelinde son 12 ayda 350 milyondan fazla müşteri tarafından kullanıldığını belirtiyor. Erdem, özelliğin kullanıcı geri bildirimleri ve yeni özelliklerle geliştirilmeye devam edeceğini de ifade ediyor.
Alexa ile Alışveriş'e mobil uygulamada ekranın sağ alt köşesinde yer alan Alexa simgesi üzerinden erişilebiliyor. Web tarafında ise Amazon.com.tr'nin üst bölümündeki Alexa alanı kullanılıyor.

LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections.
To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM. Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages.
Today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview . We are also releasing a GitHub repo, which includes a toolkit for working with LLMON and examples of workflows and templates.
JSON was designed for parsers, not for causal language models. The tokenizer is not constrained to respect the grammar, and structure is encoded by tokens ({, ", :) that may also appear in normal text. To a model, a quotation mark inside a document and a quotation mark that closes a field are the same token. Escaping rules that are clear to a parser are only statistical patterns to a model. Nesting depth is encoded by counting brackets, which transformers are known to be weak at, especially over long spans.
LLMON, on the other hand, is an XML-like markup whose structural delimiters are reserved special tokens rather than characters, so structure and content use separate parts of the vocabulary. Tags are stated at the beginning of each span, and the boundaries between spans are explicit. Nested structures are stated locally so the model does not need to keep track of the hierarchy over long spans.
Since most teams already have pipelines built around JSON, we created conversion tools and example notebooks that translate JSON to LLMON and back in a lossless manner.
LLMON does not replace chat templates; rather, it enriches them. Where regular chat templates tell the model which part belongs to which role (system, user, assistant), LLMON tells it what each component means and how components relate to each other, within and across roles.
The LLMON preview models ship with their own chat template, so you build the same messages list you would pass to any chat model and call apply_chat_template as usual; it renders the LLMON shown below. The only difference is that a turn can now name its parts and mark each one exec : True or False . A part marked True is bound into the exec block at the bottom of the rendered output, which states which instruction to run and what it operates on; a part marked False is still rendered into the context but is referenced by nothing.
Which the model receives as the following (with newlines and indentation added here for readability, as the template emits none):
The two-character block IDs are drawn from a fixed set that this tokenizer encodes as single tokens, so addressing a block always costs two tokens regardless of which ID is drawn.
The role is still a single user turn, but its components reach the model as five separate addressable blocks, bound together by a sixth (the exec block) that states: run this instruction, on this data, subject to these two requirements, and put the answer in the block named here, which is the same assistant block the model then fills. A conventional template would have flattened all components into one string and left the model to infer which part was the task, which was the subject, and which were constraints.
Indirect prompt injection is a type of attack where a malicious instruction is hidden in a data payload, such as a retrieved document, a tool response, or user-provided data. This is the problem LLMON’s instruction/data separation is designed to address.
We compared the LLMON previews against several open-source and closed-source models. We evaluated on the OPI benchmark, which places the injection in the data of classic NLP tasks. Several attack strategies are employed. We report robustness, defined as 1 − attack success rate: the share of attacks where the model does not carry out the injected instruction.
All non-LLMON models are highly susceptible, carrying out the injected instructions with high probability. LLMON practically eliminates the problem on this benchmark, avoiding 47% more attacks relative to the best frontier model that we tested, and 95% more than the best open-source model. We observe similar trends on other benchmarks ( ASB and StruQ ). It is worth noting that these benchmarks test robustness to static indirect prompt injections. The instruction/data separation directly addresses this type of attack. We are actively working on also improving adaptive attacks which unfold over many chat turns.
Safety gains don’t come at the expense of general capability. Across standard benchmark categories, the LLMON models perform on par with the Granite 4.1 Instruct models.
In short, if you’re experimenting with Granite 4.1 3B or 8B today, you can swap in the LLMON preview and should see comparable general performance with much stronger resistance to prompt injection. No conversion pipeline is required. Naming the turn's parts (e.g., instruction, data, requirement as in the example above) is enough. The shipped chat template turns those into LLMON blocks for you. Our LLMON-converters library goes one level deeper: if a part is itself structured, such as a JSON document, LLMONizing it preserves that structure as typed, individually addressable blocks, instead of one opaque string.
The models start from Granite 4.1 base checkpoints rather than the released instruct models, so LLMON behavior is learned during post-training rather than layered on an existing chat format.
LLMON defines six delimiters that mark the start and end of tags and allow nesting and anchoring; they are installed in the tokenizer as reserved single tokens. We re-serialized a conventional instruction-tuning corpus into LLMON: every prompt component becomes its own addressable block, and each turn carries an execution block naming which instruction to run, which inputs it operates on, and where the output goes. The task mix is the one a normal instruct model sees (chat, multi-turn, RAG, tool calling), which is why benchmark performance stays close to the conventionally tuned model. In addition, we augment the data with decoy instructions and data blocks that are present in context but deliberately left unbound, while the target output is unchanged. So the model learns to follow the dependencies dictated by the execution block and ignore the rest. Reinforcement learning follows: five sequential GRPO stages spanning multi-domain reasoning, RLHF, knowledge calibration, and math, followed by a final DPO stage on a thousand on-policy preference pairs built from the model’s own responses to injection attempts.

Microsoft said its Outlook email service is currently experiencing an outage, preventing users from accessing their inboxes.
The issue was initially flagged as affecting the U.S. and the Americas, and later expanded to affect “any region.”
Microsoft hasn’t given a specific cause, but said that it was providing updates in its admin center , which wasn’t reachable at the time of publication. In a post on X for users who can’t access the admin center, Microsoft said some of its infrastructure was experiencing “elevated load,” and that it was “redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load.”
The company’s last major incident was in September , when a days-long outage hit Microsoft 365, its online productivity suite that includes Outlook. During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service.
It’s unclear to what extent the outage extends to other services. TechCrunch will reach out to Microsoft for comment, as soon as our email service has resumed.

Families confront Google after teen’s lawsuit labels Gemini a “suicide coach.”
CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI.
The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried.
In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!”
Called to action by a nonprofit grassroots advocacy group, the Illinois Families for Public Schools (ILFPS), some parents and students had previously won a major AI fight. In August, the group pressured Chicago Public Schools (CPS) to pull out of a Gemini pilot that would have roped in all high school students districtwide—without consulting parents. And now, ILFPS is demanding a moratorium on AI until risks to students are better understood and CPS can draft a policy to protect students from potential learning setbacks or more harmful outcomes from engaging Google’s AI bots. If the group wins, it will join cities like Los Angeles and New York City in cautiously banning AI in schools.
Most alarming to parents, Google now faces a lawsuit from a 13-year-old student in Durham, North Carolina named “Emma Doe.” As Emma has alleged, she was a happy, well-adjusted, straight-A student when she started using Gemini on her school-issued Chromebook. Emma’s parents had no idea she was using Gemini, as the lawsuit alleged that Google “deliberately” kept them in the dark while driving Emma into so-called “AI psychosis.” Over time, normal school-related interactions with the chatbot led to more intense chats, and ultimately the chatbot allegedly coached Emma to plan her own suicide and funeral. The school warned her parents and averted the danger after an internal system flagged a chat labeled “Funeral,” but Emma’s story stoked fears of parents joining protests not just in Durham, but also in Boston; Boulder, Colorado; Chicago; Los Angeles; New York City; and Portland, Oregon.
Emma’s lawsuit accuses Google of exploiting its dominant position in education technology and “sneaking” Gemini into Chromebooks, while falsely marketing them as safe.
“As a direct consequence of Google’s choices, Emma was baited by its defectively designed products into repeated, unmonitored, sycophantic AI chatbot interactions on her school Chromebook without her parents ever knowing. And, but for a fortunate turn of events, Google’s AI may well have manipulated Emma into taking her own life,” the lawsuit alleged. “Google must be held to account for treating the lives of children as disposable in service of its bottom line.”
Google has promised to “continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning.” However, Google’s statements so far attempting to address parents’ concerns focus exclusively on documented harms to learning. On that front, Google claims that it’s solving the problem of AI eroding students’ critical thinking skills by launching yet another pilot for students. In this pilot, students using AI Mode and AI Overviews will be offered a “step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork,” Google said.
Cassie Creswell, executive director of ILFPS, told Ars that she’s been an advocate monitoring edtech issues for more than a decade. And even she was blindsided by Google’s AI moves.
“I am aware of AI Overviews when you search, which have a whole slew of problems, but I did not know that you really actually just have an interface where you can interact with Gemini in the chatbot way on everyone’s Chromebook still in Chicago public schools,” Creswell said. “And that’s so disturbing.”
She acknowledged that kids encounter AI on their phones and shared that her daughter said her friends like using ChatGPT better than Gemini. But she said that the fact that some kids use AI on personal devices doesn’t mean that schools should be encouraging adoption at young ages when kids’ brains are still developing, and risks remain largely unknown.
“There’s all kinds of dangerous things out in the world, but we don’t have our school district handing it to kids at their desk,” Creswell said.
Meanwhile, schools seem to be part of the transparency problem.
Creswell said that currently, the Chicago school district “is telling us their official line is that kids don’t have access to generative AI tools and that we don’t need a district-level policy on generative AI because they have guidebooks.” However, she’s reviewed Google’s CPS contracts, and they suggest that kids are interacting with generative AI and frontier models. The ongoing confusion has led parents to demand “a real policy” that the CPS “board votes on and that has the input of teachers, parents, students, and experts who are not being funded by the tech industry.”
Creswell told Ars that parents are particularly upset that Google is not transparent about how it processes and uses student data. She’s exhaustively researched Google contracts through Freedom of Information Act requests and told Ars that dozens of agreements she reviewed offer no indication of how CPS partners like Google—as well as Anthropic and OpenAI—are handling student data. Although she understands that “it’s probably just an honest statement of fact” that Google has built AI inextricably into Search, parents have a right to know how their children’s data is ingested into Google’s models, she said.
“Any sort of transparency on what is actually happening in terms of the data that they collect and what they do with it, that is absolutely missing,” Creswell said. And “it’s very unclear what data is being saved.”
To Creswell and other advocates, it seems likely that kids’ data is collected no matter what, since “even if you do ‘-AI,’ and you don’t get a text summary, your search data and what’s being returned is all basically inside the generative AI model.” Although Illinois law only allows commercial use of de-identified data, parents think Google should clearly explain what steps it takes to ensure data can’t be recombined to re-identify kids.
Ars reached out to Google to see if the company could clarify if Creswell’s read is accurate or if there’s any meaningful distinction between adding “-AI” to an individual query versus building a button that would automatically add “-AI” to every query. Google did not clarify, instead emphasizing that schools will control whether students can access the Gemini app, Gemini Notebook, and Search, with options to toggle each off individually, but no option to use Search without AI.
Emma Doe’s lawsuit alleged that Google has taken advantage of a dominant position it has held in schools since 2007 to push AI on kids and seize their data without meaningfully protecting them from the worst potential harms of its chatbot’s sycophantic design . In Chicago, CPS signed a contract with Google in 2020, “long before Gemini was rolled out,” Creswell found. Over the next two extensions of that contract, no updates were introduced to protect students’ privacy as AI advanced.
To Creswell, it remained “totally unclear” in contracts how Google’s processing of student data may have changed, beyond updates to the privacy policy for Google Workspace for Education.

Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue briefly commented on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday, calling it a “really sad day.” Nvidia had announced its plan to acquire the platform for open source AI models in September for $12.9 billion, making it the second-largest acquisition in the company’s history, just behind that of chipmaker Groq’s assets for $20 billion in December 2025.
“This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!,” Delangue wrote on X.
This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!
The post is interesting as it implies that Huang’s departure is potentially worrying to open source advocates, and he’s attempting to offer reassurance.
As Nvidia’s CEO, Huang was known as a strong advocate for open source AI and open-weight models, which is why there could be concerns about how a company that’s no longer under his leadership will now approach this space.
After Nvidia announced its plans to acquire Hugging Face, the U.S. Department of Justice began making inquiries about how the deal would impact competition in the AI market, Reuters reported in October . While Nvidia pledged that the platform would preserve open support, it would also allow the company to control a major distribution channel for AI models.
The Hugging Face deal is still scheduled to close in the first half of 2027. Requests for further comment on the deal status and whether Hugging Face has spoken yet with Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress were not returned.
Huang’s advocacy for open source and open-weight AI has long extended beyond Hugging Face. In July, the CEO published an AI policy letter as his first-ever post on the social network X . The letter, which was signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, Hugging Face, IBM, Palantir, and others, urged the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models. It said models that “anyone can download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure” are an important part of the AI ecosystem because they make AI “more accessible, adaptable, and widely available.”
Huang also wrote that open-weight models expand access to the AI economy, strengthen competition, and give customers greater control, as they know they won’t become locked into a single provider. “Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” his post on X stated.
For my first post, I’m sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter. AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country. Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty.… pic.twitter.com/t02bi51N4C
In August, Nvidia also announced a $6 billion deal with the coding startup Poolside to help build out an open AI ecosystem in the U.S. to help the country compete against Chinese companies like DeepSeek and Kimi K3, The Wall Street Journal reported at the time. Last month, Nvidia expanded its Nemotron family of open-weight models with a large 120-billion-parameter model for agents used by the enterprise as well as with two new lightweight Bolt models that run on PCs.
Earlier this year, Huang promoted open source AI during his January keynote address at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, noting that open source models have “really revolutionized artificial intelligence.”

New research published in Science on Thursday shows that the conditions that have kept ice, frozen soil, and snow stable are slipping away due to the burning of fossil fuels—and the implications are grave for the entire globe .
The climate of the past 12,000 or so years has been remarkably steady. That’s allowed for all kinds of wonderful things to happen, like human civilization flourishing. But rising temperatures are pushing the climate outside that envelope , and the new research looks at what the team behind the new findings has called the “safe operating space” for the icy, snowy landscape known as the cryosphere.
The scientists looked at changes to polar sea and land ice, mountain glaciers, permafrost, and snow cover over the past 12 millennia to analyze conditions that have allowed both civilization and other ecosystems to thrive. They then identified boundaries on those conditions that, if crossed, would upend the stability and safety humans have enjoyed for millennia.
The results show an “accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity.” Arctic and Antarctic sea ice have both fallen outside the safe operating threshold, as have snow cover and the area of permafrost—frozen soil laden with carbon. While land ice hasn’t yet fallen out of its safe space, it’s on the brink. And because of warming that’s already been locked into the climate system, it’s likely to also fall outside the threshold in the coming centuries.
While it may feel like the Antarctic ice sheet or permafrost covering Alaska are distant concerns, they’re anything but. The West Antarctic Ice Sheet, which a growing body of evidence shows is nearing the brink of irreversible decline , has enough ice to raise sea levels by 11 feet (3 meters). Permafrost, meanwhile, holds trillions of tons of carbon dioxide. Any degradation means that CO2, as well as even more potent methane, could end up in the atmosphere , accelerating global warming even further. Other examples of major risks abound, including how melting Greenland land ice could slow down or even collapse the ocean conveyor belt that helps keep Europe temperate.
“The consequences of a changing cryosphere extend beyond regions where ice and snow are disappearing,” says Albert Noström, a climate researcher at the Stockholm Resilience Center who co-authored the new paper.
Dipping outside the safe operating space doesn’t mean that the world will see 11 feet of sea level rise in the next year, a trillion-ton CO2 eruption, or a Day After Tomorrow scenario. But it does mean that the odds of crossing dangerous tipping points are rising.
“As we scratch 1.5 [degrees Celsius] and go above it, we are just really gambling with potentially triggering some of these Earth system tipping points,” Noström says. The safe operating space framework also “takes a broader perspective” that assesses slower changes over time and “how far, in this case, the cryosphere is moving away from the conditions that have supported a relatively stable Earth system,” he adds.
Cutting emissions is the most obvious and straightforward way to stop the cryosphere from sliding further outside our comfort zone. But there are a growing number of proposals to pursue more radical interventions that could protect the world’s ice. Scientists have already draped glaciers in the Alps in blankets during the summer to prevent melting. Other researchers have explored techniques to pump cold sea water to the surface to help thicken ice and modeled whether a manmade barrier could stabilize the West Antarctic Ice Sheet.
These geoengineering approaches have the potential to be costly, and there’s no guarantee they would work. They’d also do nothing to stop the root cause of warming: burning fossil fuels. Noström says emissions cuts are the most urgent way to protect ice and snow (and ourselves), but with the cryosphere sliding into a more dangerous space, “in principle, we shouldn't put the lid on” research for more far-flung interventions.
“The safe operating space is a precautionary framework,” he says. “It ensures that we try to stay as far downstream from the point where these really potentially existential or huge consequences and risks can happen.”

We caught the first trailer for the upcoming Netflix animated film Ray Gunn in September and were charmed by director Brad Bird’s blend of a Jetsons-like future with classic 1930s noir detective thrillers. Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers , and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy.
As previously reported , Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He’s been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year.
The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “ Planet Claire ” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn . Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a pun on “ raygun ,” of course). “It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird .
Per the official premise: “In Metropia, a gigantic city in an alternate future as seen from 1939, private eye Raymond Gunn (voiced by Sam Rockwell) is drawn into a case involving aliens, murder, and a multimedia star named Venus Nova (voiced by Scarlett Johansson).”
Unlike Bird’s Pixar fare, Ray Gunn targets a slightly older demographic with more mature themes.
In addition to Rockwell and Johansson, the all-star voice cast includes Tom Waits as Ray’s one-eyed alien colleague, Eyera (pronounced Ira); Matt Berry as alien mob boss Francis “Sluggy” Xavier; Bobby Cannavale as Venus’ husband, who hires Ray to spy on his wife; Alan Tudyk as Venus’ manager, Barry Vogel; Michael Chernus as a studio fixer named Sam; and Patton Oswalt as a hologram. Bird himself provides the voices for Xavier’s alien henchmen, Gunsol and Musker. Kathryn Hunter, John Ratzenberger, and Jamie Costa will also voice as-yet-undisclosed characters.
Ray Gunn releases on Netflix on December 18, 2026—the same day both Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3 hit theaters, so it will be alternative family fare for those disinclined to brave the holiday theatrical crowds. The film will also screen in select theaters on December 4, 2026.
